shortName: Robert Larner, M.D., College of Medicine at the University of Vermont
additionalCoursework: Recommended courses: Genetics, Biostatistics, Anatomy, Physiology, Molecular Biology, and Microbiology. We encourage students to have a broad and balanced educational background during their undergraduate years. In addition to courses in the sciences, recommended areas of study include literature, mathematics, behavioral sciences, history, philosophy, and the arts.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
Our commitment to diversity at the Larner College of Medicine runs deep. We value diversity as a driver of excellence and support the education of physicians and scientists who will go on to serve, and thrive in a multicultural local and global community. We know that in today's society, our future physicians need a level of cultural competence that spans the globe. 

We believe that diversity leads to excellence and is an asset in teaching, research and patient care. These values have implications for our students as they go on to practice: Fostering a community of scholars and clinicians from different backgrounds provides the richest set of viewpoints for decision-making in health care. Our students graduate as culturally competent medical professionals ready for the challenges of ensuring health equity in our global society.

We embrace diversity in its broadest forms, encompassing the intersectionality of identities that define an individual's lived experiences.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Upon certain provisions, a student may be granted a leave of absence by the Associate Dean for  Student Affairs.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: UVM students are encouraged to find a balance between working hard and relaxation. Our location on the campus of the state's flagship university provides students with a wealth of educational and recreational opportunities.  Our students participate in a wide variety of activities, including interest groups in medical specialties, global health, medical Spanish, wilderness medicine and intramural sports to name a few. Our Connecticut campus is close to New York City with easy access to all the amenities of one of the largest cities in the US.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located in Burlington, VT, the University of Vermont campus is home to more than 11,000 students, faculty and staff. Burlington is a vibrant community located on the shores of Lake Champlain, between the Adirondack and Green Mountains, and regularly ranks at the top of the best places to live lists. With year-round recreational opportunities, this progressive community is within a half-day's drive of Boston and New York, and Montreal is just 100 miles north of campus. The Larner College of Medicine and teaching partner The University of Vermont Medical Center comprise the only academic medical center in Vermont, which creates opportunities to interact with physicians, educators, and policy-makers at all levels around the state.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Medical students share apartments or houses in the surrounding area. Many housing opportunities are within easy walking or bicycling distance from campus.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Gender and Sexuality Alliance's purpose is to foster a nurturing and supportive environment for students identifying with the sexuality and gender spectrums and their allies, and to ensure all students have the skills and resources to become skilled health care providers for people of all genders and sexual orientations. The GSA is also a member of the Medical Student Pride Alliance (MSPA), serving as the Vermont Chapter.  The MSPA is a national organization that connects LGBTQ medical students across the country and provides professional resources for these students as they begin their careers.

medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At Larner College of Medicine, we foster a campus culture that celebrates inclusivity, collaboration, and respect, creating an environment where everyone feels valued and supported in their pursuit of excellence. Our community is united by a shared commitment to professionalism, integrity, and mutual respect, reflected in our interactions with peers, faculty, staff, and the broader community. We promote a culture of belonging where diverse perspectives are welcomed and we hold each other accountable for upholding the highest ethical standards. By cultivating an environment rooted in kindness, compassion, and open-mindedness, we enhance our educational and clinical practices and collective growth as compassionate leaders in medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Regardless of a student's clinical campus, they must travel for their rotations. Public transportation is not available to get students to the various locations, and a personal vehicle is required. Exceptions can be made if needed as an accommodation determined by the Student Accessibility Service Unit.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Business casual or scrubs when in the operating room.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Small groups, lectures and team-based learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Rotations begin in mid-March of the second year of medical school. 35 students will transfer to our CT clinical campus to complete the last two years of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: A three-week-long online or in-person program is available in July 2026 for all entering students.  It is designed to familiarize students with our environment and review critical content.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Varies from course to course. The most successful students are those who attend all of our active learning opportunities.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Vermont Integrated Curriculum (VIC) progresses from the study of Foundations of Medicine, both clinical and basic science, to applications in Clinical Clerkship, to senior scholarship and supervised patient management in Advanced Integration. Areas of focus include progressive skill development, health care systems, preventive care, and a greater understanding of applied sciences, particularly genetics, ethics and epidemiology. The VIC also places emphasis on professionalism, cultural competency, scholarly research, teaching skills, and community service. The curriculum is transitioning to 100 percent active learning. By replacing lectures with active learning at Larner, we aim to help students think critically and apply foundational knowledge to the types of clinical situations they will face as physicians.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: We are located in a rural state and advancing access to our communities is of utmost importance to us. Our AHEC office is strongly committed to increasing access to primary care for our communities. Please visit our website for more details.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students are able to apply for research fellowships in the summer between first and second year of their medical studies. Other research opportunities outside of this internship exist  at the medical school and the larger UVM campus.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Please see our website for a complete description of our curriculum's three levels. Pass curriculum in all four years with honors option in the fourth year.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students interact with the community in various ways, and the most significant is the Public Health Research projects, which take place in the fall of the second year.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students are required to complete a Scholarly Project, which can be research or teaching. Students pick one or the other depending on their career goals. It is possible to do both.

medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
We celebrate over 200 years of excellence in educating physicians and physician-scientists, and in serving our local and global community.

The mission of the Larner College of Medicine at The University of Vermont is to educate a diverse group of dedicated physicians and biomedical scientists to serve across all the disciplines of medicine; to bring hope to patients by advancing medical knowledge through research; to integrate education and research to advance the quality and accessibility of patient care; and to engage with our communities to benefit Vermont and the world. We achieve this mission through: 

Admissions: Mission aligned 
Mission Aligned Selection and Retention Process: Our applicant screening, interview, and acceptance processes are guided by our mission. Each matriculating student demonstrates excellence in one or more of the specific tenets of our mission, whether through research, experience with rural and disadvantaged communities, or a significant commitment to the betterment of humanity. At the core of our university is a strong mission for social justice, which appears in our medical school's mission. Because we value the unique benefits of social learning, our interview day includes a team-based activity to help our candidates become familiar with this teaching approach.

Student Affairs: Individualized- Timely- Compassionate 
A strong, interdisciplinary, and robust team of student support professionals that "hold" our students as soon as they commit to the first day of Orientation until the day they are hooded and earn their MD. The team includes Personal Health & Well-being, Academic Support, & Intensive Career Planning, spanning both of our campuses. 

Curriculum: Innovative- Learner Centered- Engaging- Relevant
Our active learning approach to instruction is built on adult learning principles and proven educational pedagogy. Our students construct knowledge through a variety of teaching modalities. Larner provides rural and urban clinical opportunities on two campuses in Vermont and Connecticut, where our learners engage with diverse patient populations. Our two-campus model also allows students to select an academic (VT) or community (CT) setting for their clinical rotations. Each student is required to complete a community-focused public health project in their first year, which positions them to learn how to be present in a community, because this is their passion. Check out our website for additional curricular opportunities!

The secret to achieving our mission is our well-defined culture of professionalism. Each student who is admitted to Larner can expect to enter a community that is committed to a culture of professionalism: 
Our Larner College of Medicine community upholds the highest standards of professionalism as we pursue lifelong learning and improvement. We demonstrate professionalism through integrity, accountability, compassion, altruism, and social responsibility. We honor the trust our society has placed in us as stewards of the art and science of medicine, guided by cultural humility, kindness, and respect in our daily interactions. We expect all members of our community to embrace these principles of professionalism as we strive to conduct and support patient care, research, and education that are second to none.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks unless there are extenuating circumstances.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: All letters must be submitted through the AMCAS letter writer portal. We do not accept letters submitted directly to the admissions office.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: If your institution provides a Committee Letter, it is preferred. If you do not have a Committee Letter, you may submit three academic or professional letters from people who know you well and can speak to your character and intellectual curiosity.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: The Larner College of Medicine will be offering virtual interviews. We hope to convey the collaborative and supportive environment of our campus to you through a variety of pre-recorded webinars, live zoom sessions, and the interview day activities.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Multiple mini-interviews with faculty, community leaders, and students. Candidates will also participate in a groujp problem solving activity.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Regional interviews are not available. All interviews are conducted online.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Our interviews will be virtual for the 2026-2027 cycle.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: A meeting with the Associate Dean for Admissions is required for preapproval to apply to our program. We want to ensure applicants are aware of all considerations for this decision.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: More than 70 percent of students are from out of state.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Students are responsible for finding funding sources. Only partial scholarships available.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
1. We will accept Pass/Satisfactory grades for prerequisite courses
2. We do accept online courses and labs
3. We require accepted students to PTE by April 30, 2027, to retain their seat
4. We require accepted students to CTE by June 28, 2027, to retain their seat
5. We do not have a seat deposit
6. The secondary application fee is waived for all applicants who receive FAP. If you were not eligible for FAP please email our office.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The committee considers all scores, with primary emphasis on the highest score. Applicants who show a significant decline in their MCAT score have historically required additional support to be successful in their courses and on their exams.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: We do not have a threshold for the MCAT. Students with a 502 or higher have historically succeeded in our curriculum and national standardized exams.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: A gpa of  3.0 or higher in the sciences is generally related to high success in our curriculum.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: We do not have an undergraduate gpa cut off to consider the graduate gpa. We will consider graduate gpa or post bacc when an applicant has completed those credits. Applicants are encouraged to complete science coursework if they were challenged in science and math during their undergraduate journey.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: If an applicant completes a potbacc or graduate course work we prefer to see science courses.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We do not differentiate between community college and university coursework.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
We encourage applicants to submit updates and letters of interest via our application portal in PDF format. There is no limit to the number of documents you can upload, so please feel free to share as many relevant updates as you need.

We highly recommend submitting letters of intent and keeping us informed by uploading updates regularly. This is an excellent way to share your ongoing interest throughout the application process.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
The University of Vermont (UVM) Larner College of Medicine (LCOM) is an educationally purposeful and welcoming community that strives to attract and educate students who will demonstrate professionalism through our core values of integrity, accountability, compassion, altruism, and social responsibility, and rely on cultural humility, kindness, and respect to guide our daily interactions. 

The Larner College of Medicine’s Technical Standards include essential academic and non-academic abilities, attributes, and characteristics in the areas of 1) intellectual-conceptual, integrative, and quantitative abilities; 2) observational skills; 3) communication (verbal and non-verbal); 4) motor function (gross and fine muscular movements, balance, and equilibrium); 5) emotional resilience; 6) behavioral and social skills; and 7) ethics and professionalism.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial aid funds are distributed according to relative need for both in and out-of-state students. Entering students are considered for awards on the same basis as those already enrolled. An applicant's financial status has no bearing on the admission determination.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Register and take CASPer between May and December. Applications with no CASPer score are not considered for interview
We require accepted students to Plan to Enroll by April 30, 2026 to retain their seat

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation: The CASPer must be taken before an interview invitation is extended. Applications are considered complete when CASPer test registration is confirmed. The score is used in pre-screening for interviews.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Our Waitlist is active until the class matriculates. No updates are needed from applicants on the waitlist and can be helpful. Once the waitlist is closed, applicants will be notified by email.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
One year (or 8 credits) of each of the following college-level courses is required: Biology (including laboratory), Physics (including laboratory), General or inorganic chemistry (including laboratory), Organic chemistry (including laboratory), and Biochemistry. We also strongly recommend that at least one molecular genetics course be taken.

The College of Medicine strongly encourages its prospective students to concentrate while in college in a field of knowledge of their choice, whether in the sciences or humanities, and to pursue their interests in depth. 

College work must demonstrate intellectual drive, independent thinking, curiosity, and self-discipline. A career in medicine calls for excellent oral and written communication skills. Applicants should seek out opportunities to develop such skills during their college years. Successful applicants often have a history of service to their community
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no expiration date on coursework.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Our mission-aligned selection and retention admissions approach includes a thorough review of each application for evidence of excellence, accompanied by genuine concern for the welfare of others. We value strong interpersonal skills and look for applicants with a history of community service. Selection is based on a past pattern of academic performance and an assessment of the applicant's fitness for the study and practice of medicine, including aptitude, interests, experience, motivation, leadership abilities, and maturity. Letters of recommendation and a multiple mini interview are required and form an important part of the application process. The Larner College of Medicine seeks a diverse student body.  We highly encourage students from groups historically underrepresented in medicine to apply.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We are sensitive to and appreciative of how difficult shadowing experiences are to find. We do not require shadowing experience of any applicant. We value all clinical experiences that applicants have had that have informed their understanding of medicine as a profession.
